shortDescription: Cambium Bio ASX:CMB has pushed back the start of its pivotal Phase 3 trial of Elate Ocular to the first quarter of 2027 as it prepares for commercial partnering discussions in San Francisco in January.The regenerative medicine developer now expects manufacturing of the drug for the CAMOMILE-2 study…

children: Cambium Bio
has pushed back the start of its pivotal Phase 3 trial of Elate Ocular to the first quarter of 2027 as it prepares for commercial partnering discussions in San Francisco in January.

The regenerative medicine developer now expects manufacturing of the drug for the CAMOMILE-2 study in moderate to severe dry eye disease to continue into early 2027, with patient enrolment previously scheduled to begin by the end of 2026.
The revised timetable puts the release of initial headline trial results in the first quarter of 2028 rather than the final quarter of 2027.
Cambium Bio is now targeting the second half of 2028 for submission of a Biologics License Application to the US Food and Drug Administration, compared with its previous mid-2028 target.
Single Trial Registration Strategy
The company is pursuing a single registration-enabling Phase 3 trial following feedback from the FDA, which granted Elate Ocular fast-track designation in 2024.
CAMOMILE-2 is designed to randomise 515 patients between the investigational eye drops and a control solution without the active ingredient, with 475 patients expected to be evaluable.
The study will assess corneal surface damage and patient-reported eye discomfort after nine weeks of treatment, followed by a 12-month open-label safety extension involving 100 patients.
Cambium Bio has identified eight potential trial sites in Australia and three in the US, although site contracts have yet to be executed and the network remains subject to change.
Human Donor Platelets

Elate Ocular is derived from pooled human donor platelets using Cambium Bio’s proprietary Aurarix technology, which removes the clot-forming protein fibrinogen while retaining growth factors involved in tissue repair.
The formulation is designed to replicate key components of natural tears without requiring patients to undergo blood collection for personalised serum eye drops.
An earlier randomised Phase 1/2 trial involving 64 patients with severe dry eye associated with chronic ocular graft-versus-host disease met its primary safety endpoints.

The higher 30% concentration produced statistically significant improvements in six of nine symptom measures compared with the control after 42 days, including a 33-point relative improvement in eye discomfort on a 100-point scale.

Investigators recorded no treatment-related adverse events at that concentration, while the study was not designed with sufficient statistical power to establish effects on clinical signs of the disease.
Commercial Partnering Focus
Cambium Bio has invested more than $35 million in Elate Ocular development and recently completed a $7.1m placement that settled on 18 November.

The company estimates that only around 7% of the 16.4 million diagnosed US dry eye patients receive prescription therapy, with about 90% of patients who start treatment discontinuing their initial prescription within a year.
Commercial protection could extend into the 2040s through a combination of patent protection and 12 years of US regulatory exclusivity from first approval, should the product gain FDA clearance.

Cambium Bio will attend Biotech Showcase and BIO Partnering at JPM during the J.P. Morgan Healthcare Conference week from 11 to 14 January 2027, with discussions centred on Elate Ocular, and intends to pursue out-licensing of the treatment or a potential sale of the business once Phase 3 begins.

title: Cambium Bio Postpones Pivotal Dry Eye Trial Ahead of Talks re Commercial Partnering
